title: Oklahoma 17, Nebraska 14: Thanksgiving 1972 Comeback in Lincoln
question: How did Oklahoma beat Nebraska 17-14 on Thanksgiving Day in 1972?
answer: Down 14-0 in the third quarter, Oklahoma scored 17 straight points, capped by Rich Fulcher's 41-yard field goal, to beat Nebraska 17-14 in Lincoln on November 23, 1972, in Bob Devaney's last home game.
summary: On Thanksgiving 1972, Oklahoma rallied from a 14-0 deficit at Nebraska behind Joe Washington, Grant Burget and Rich Fulcher's 41-yard field goal to win 17-14.
body: For decades the Oklahoma-Nebraska game was a Thanksgiving-week fixture, and the 1972 edition on November 23 in Lincoln was a gem. It came a year after the famous 35-31 "Game of the Century" in Norman, and this time the Sooners were the ones chasing.

Nebraska struck first. Bill Olds ran 14 yards for a first-quarter touchdown, and Dave Goeller added a 1-yard score in the third quarter to make it 14-0. A crowd of 76,587 braved a 31-degree afternoon, and Oklahoma trailed by two touchdowns.
The turn came late in the third quarter, when Joe Washington punched in from a yard out to cut the lead to 14-7. Early in the fourth, Grant Burget scored from a yard out, and the game was tied.

The decisive play was a defensive one. Oklahoma sacked Nebraska quarterback Dave Humm and forced a fumble, which gave the Sooners the ball in field goal range. On fourth down, kicker Rich Fulcher kicked a 41-yard field goal to make it 17-14. Nebraska never answered.

The win carried extra weight because it was Bob Devaney's final home game as Nebraska's head coach, and Oklahoma spoiled it. It was also Chuck Fairbanks's last regular season at Oklahoma, since he left afterward for the NFL's New England Patriots.
